rationale_overall: Filtered a large volume of noise this week: private/non-investable nuclear names (Westinghouse, Radiant DOE microreactor selection), a Canadian junior uranium explorer with no liquid US line (North Shore Uranium), a China state uranium project, foreign/OTC names (Samsung, Huawei chip stories), unrelated satellite stories (Bezos-backed MethaneSAT loss, Israeli Dror 1 launch, astronomy/volcano satellite imagery, Melrose brand awards, a Missile Command video game), geopolitical missile/attack reporting with no tradeable equity attached (Iran-Qatar, Yemen-Israel, Taiwan HIMARS), and vague clickbait 'this AI stock' pieces that never name a ticker. NVDA's chip-export and $4T-cap coverage reaffirms the current AI wave but changes nothing about the existing holding. The one genuine catalyst — Rocket Lab (RKLB), up 33.5% last month and continuing to surge, a real rockets & spacecraft wave vehicle — is real but reads more like a stock already mid-run than early buildup, and per this run's rule an add requires a paired remove; none of AAPL/GOOGL/MSFT/NVDA show a peaking or thesis-breach signal strong enough to justify swapping out a core AI holding for a single week's momentum print. Watchlist held unchanged this period.
